subject: BrightPath onboarding — model shortlist & token projection
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@brightpath.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: BrightPath onboarding: model shortlist & token projection

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're ready to start the technical onboarding and need Redwood's recommendations for a model shortlist and an initial sizing estimate so we can budget committed capacity. High level: BrightPath will use the model for two features initially — (1) document Q&A over customer-uploaded PDFs, and (2) concise executive summaries of multi-page reports. A few specifics to help scope: 

- Expected pilot window: Q3 (launch to ~1,200 customers over 3 months).
- Monthly active users during pilot: ~12,000 (we expect uneven day-of-week traffic).
- Usage per active user (pilot average): ~8 queries/month (mix of Q&A and summaries).
- Typical prompt payloads: 600–4,500 tokens. Most Q&A rounds attach a 2,500–10,000-token document as context (we can send samples).
- Desired response sizes: 150–800 tokens depending on summary vs Q&A.
- SLOs: p95 response time < 500ms for Q&A short-form flows; summaries can tolerate up to 1.5s.
- Data residency: US only.

Questions / asks for Redwood:
1) Shortlist three model configurations to validate (tradeoffs: cost vs quality vs max context).
2) Recommended context window(s) to support without rewriting the product UX.
3) Rough monthly token estimates and an initial recommendation on hosted vs reserved capacity at pilot scale.
4) Any constraints on document chunking, KV-cache usage, or pre-processing that we should plan for.

I've attached a small CSV with anonymized document-size distribution and a one-page usage projection (sample_docs_metadata.csv). We're happy to run a short sample payload test if you want to validate throughput.

Appreciate a preliminary reply this week — can do a 30–60m technical workshop after that.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Platform
BrightPath Analytics

Attachments: sample_docs_metadata.csv (CSV, 1.1MB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightPath onboarding: model shortlist & token projection

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the sample CSV. This is a great starting point. I've looped in Ben (workload modeling) and Monica (CS implementation) so we can give you a concise shortlist and a sizing back-of-envelope. Below is a short preliminary recommendation we can refine during the workshop.

Preliminary model shortlist (tradeoffs):
- Option A: redwood-13b-8k-q4f (balanced) — strong cost/quality for typical Q&A and 8k context; highest throughput per GPU for pilot workloads.
- Option B: redwood-70b-24k-q8 (high-context) — recommended only for long-document summaries and customers that need full 24k token windows. Higher cost, fewer concurrent RPS per GPU.
- Option C: open-neox-20b-16k (open model for cost-sensitive pilots) — lower incremental cost, acceptable for extractive Q&A but less reliable on abstractive summaries.

Context recommendations:
- Default UX: support up to 8k native context (covers ~78% of your sample docs).
- Long-doc mode: enable a 24k path for >10k token documents (can be routed to a different model pool).
- Where possible, send only the relevant document passages (we can help with an extract+summarize pre-pass to trim context).

Initial capacity note (very rough):
- Pilot MAU 12k × 8 requests/month = 96k requests/month.
- If avg request payload (prompt + doc tokens included after trimming) ~2,400 tokens and response ~400 tokens => ~2400 + 400 = 2,800 tokens/request => ~269M tokens/month.

We recommend a short workshop (45 minutes) to review: sample payloads, which customers need 24k context, and whether you want predictable latency (Reserved/Dedicated) vs lower upfront cost (Hosted). I've attached our onboarding checklist to help the CS/eng teams.

Proposed times for a session: Wed 6/13 10:00–11:00 PT, Thu 6/14 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works best?

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: BrightPath onboarding: model shortlist & token projection

Grace — capturing a few quick calculations based on Elena's numbers and your provisional assumptions. Sharing so we have a baseline to present in the workshop.

Assumptions we used:
- Pilot MAU: 12,000; avg requests per MAU during pilot: 8/month => 96,000 requests/month.
- Distribution: 70% Q&A (smaller prompts), 30% long summaries (larger prompts).
- Q&A average: prompt 1,200 tokens + doc context after trimming 1,300 tokens; response 250 tokens => ~2,750 tokens/request.
- Summary average: prompt 600 tokens + doc context 8,000 tokens (no trimming) ; response 700 tokens => ~9,300 tokens/request.

Monthly token calc: 
- Q&A: 96k * 0.7 * 2,750 = 185,280,000 tokens
- Summaries: 96k * 0.3 * 9,300 = 267,840,000 tokens
- Total ≈ 453,120,000 tokens/month (pilot)

Throughput/SLO sizing (pilot peak):
- Peak qps estimate: assume peak hour 8% of daily requests concentrated into an hour => conservative peak qps ~ 40–60 RPS.
- If using redwood-13b-8k-q4f: estimated steady concurrency per GPU ~ 60–80 tokens/ms effective; we should provision for ~8–10 GPUs in Dedicated mode to meet p95 < 500ms for Q&A and < 1.5s for summaries (depends on batching and exact traffic shape).

Notes & mitigations:
- KV / prefix caching will help for repeated document queries — if you can surface document identifiers we can cache embeddings/KV and cut token throughput by ~15–30% for repeated reads.
- Where full 24k context is required, route to a smaller subset of traffic or a different model pool to avoid blocking the main 8k pool.
- Consider chunk-and-embed pre-pass for very long docs: store semantic slices and only retrieve + rehydrate top-k slices as context. This reduces token use dramatically but requires additional infra (embedding store + retrieval).

I'll drop a compact workbook with the calculation rows for the deck (workload_calc_sheet.xlsx). We can tweak numbers in the workshop once we see sample payloads.

—Ben
Principal Product Analyst, Redwood Inference
